question: Kirti starts from point A and walks 1 km towards east. She takes a right turn and walks 2 km. She then takes a left turn and walks 3 km. She takes a right turn and walks 4 km. She takes a left turn and walks 5 km. She takes a final left turn and walks 6 km to reach a point B. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should she walk in order to reach point A again? (All turns are 90 degree turns only unless specified otherwise.)
solution:
Given:

Kirti starts from point A and walks 1 km towards east.

She takes a right turn and walks 2 km.

She then takes a left turn and walks 3 km.

She takes a right turn and walks 4 km.

She takes a left turn and walks 5 km.

She takes a final left turn and walks 6 km to reach a point B. 

Based on the given conditions, we get the direction distance diagram as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e1c517a1c50f81c2c841529dc98ef1d4b76687e7f8c5f93fae3dcc3ada297dd8.png] 

Therefore, we see that in order to go from Point B to Point A again, she has to walk (1+3+5) = 9 km towards the West.

Hence, the correct answer is "**Option 1".**
